activities.title: Count the beans
parentPrompts: Count a small handful of beans together, touching each bean once as you say each number.
Ask: "How many beans are there?" When they finish counting, say the last number again: "There are 6 beans."
Ask them to put exactly 5 beans in a cup. Check by counting together.
Mix up the beans and count again. Do you get the same number?

activities.title: Make a pattern you can eat
materials: two kinds of snack pieces (e.g. two cereals or two fruits)
parentPrompts: Start a pattern: red, blue, red, blue. Ask: "What comes next?"
Let them add pieces and say the pattern out loud as they go.
Swap roles: they start a pattern and you guess what comes next.
Try a new pattern, such as red, red, blue, red, red, blue.

activities.title: Read a rhyming book and hunt for rhymes
parentPrompts: Read the book once for fun, pausing before the rhyming word so they can fill it in.
On a second read, ask: "Which two words sounded the same at the end?"
Play a quick game: "Does cat rhyme with hat? Does cat rhyme with dog?"

activities.title: Find things that start with a sound
parentPrompts: Pick one letter and say its sound (not its name). For example, "mmm" for M.
Gather objects around the house that start with that sound and put them in the basket.
Hold up each object and say its name, stretching the first sound: "mmmmug".
Ask them to say the sound and point to the letter in a book or on a card.
